body: Fell 99.6% from ₹430.92 (Jan 2008) to ₹1.51 (Mar 2020). Policy tailwind pattern like winners, but debt-funded expansion + share loss to foreign rivals. Lesson: debt and capital allocation separate winners from failures.
title: Suzlon: same tailwind, debt destroyed it

body: IPO Mar 2018 at ₹1,215 (≈₹607 after the 2023 1:2 split). IPO buyers then fell −56% to ₹251 (May 2020) and waited about three years to break even. From ₹251 → ATH ₹5,552 (Jul 2024) ≈22x: trailing P/E 6.3 → 48.7 (7.7x) × implied EPS ~2.9x, so about 66% of the log-return was rerating. Drawdowns: −47% (Aug–Oct 2020), −44% (Jul 2024–Feb 2025). ₹4,760 on 19 Nov 2026 (−14%); EPS kept rising (FY24 ₹114 → TTM ₹143), so P/E is ~33. Early signal: in 2020 it was a monopoly military-aircraft maker at 6–11x P/E with OPM rising from 15% to 25%. On 13 Jan 2021 the CCS cleared and on 3 Feb 2021 the government signed a ₹48k cr (₹45,696 cr + infrastructure) contract for 83 Tejas Mk1A, a public, multi-year revenue signal. Margins then reached ~30%. The Motilal Oswal 2020–25 wealth-creation study ranked HAL the most consistent and best all-round wealth creator. Companion BEL: ₹19.9 (May 2020) → ₹468 (Mar 2026) ≈23.5x, EPS ~5.2x, P/E 12.8 → 57. Lesson: the policy plus a single-digit-P/E monopoly drove the rerating, while continuing EPS growth (unlike the shipyards) kept the drawdown after the peak moderate.

data.ended: not ended; P/E normalised 49→33 with EPS growth
data.lesson: rerating + continuing EPS holds; IPO buyers needed patience
